attempted_axis: Exact-drive re-screen of the stale bulk-import park. Aligned-fnasm decode found a HARD BLOCKER the old park never named: our build allocated TEN callee-saved registers (`stmw r22,144(r1)`) against the target's NINE (`stmw r23,148(r1)`), so the function could never be byte-exact regardless of register colouring. The extra web was the blit pointer `bp`, a function-scope `register u32*` reused at five sites; the target materialises it into SCRATCH r6 at +0x108 (`add r6,r31,r25`, consumed by `stw r3,392(r6)` and `lwz r3,392(r6)`). Block-scoping `bp` to the six-iteration tile loop restored the target's saved-register set exactly.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.dead-local-identity-reuse-flips-callee-saved-coloring SCREENED and drove the whole investigation (residual reduced to callee-saved webs holding each other's registers); its literal remedy - deleting a dead local and reusing another - was tried by removing the genuinely unused `register BtnView* bv` and REGRESSED real 30 -> 44, so the law's remedy does not generalise to an unused-but-live-valued alias. claim.law.declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule and claim.law.independent-statement-reorder-matches-target-schedule screened: both ordering axes (assignment order of wg vs the zero locals; declaration order of x vs wg) measured NEUTRAL, and the declaration axis was re-run AFTER the saved-register set was fixed per the alignment-sensitivity rule and measured NEUTRAL again - two identical A/Bs, axis dead. claim.law.point-of-use-single-use-pointer-delay screened: dropping `register` from bp NEUTRAL; inlining bp to the direct `(&b[i])[98]` form REGRESSED real 30 -> 147 and ADDED an instruction (385 -> 386) by killing the address CSE. claim.law.reload-vs-cache-liveness screened against the +0x558 cluster and found NOT applicable: the target reloads gDiag_D04 for the call argument at +0x56c exactly as we do, so the divergence is only which scratch register holds the dead-after-compare test value.
attributes.residual: PARKED on ONE named mechanism. Saved-register set, frame (0xB8/184) and opcode multiset now all match (IDENTICAL 385/385); operand-differing rows fell 58 -> 15. What remains is a single closed permutation of four callee-saved webs that both scoring metrics normalise away as a bijective renaming (fndiff --clean real 34 and objdiff fuzzy 99.7662% are UNCHANGED across the fix): target x=r29 / wg=r28 / old=r24 versus ours x=r28 / wg=r29 / old=r23, at rows +0x20, +0x2c, +0x210, +0x218, +0x234, +0x28c, +0x370, +0x380, +0x3c8 (plus scratch r4/r5 at +0x20c/+0x21c). Two independent scratch-choice rows remain where the target parks a dead-after-compare loaded global in an allocatable GPR and we use r0: +0x3c4/+0x3cc (`lwz r4,gDiag_F4` then `slwi r0,r4,4` vs `lwz r0` then `slwi r0,r0,4`) and +0x558/+0x55c (`lwz r3,gDiag_D04` / `cmplwi r3,0` vs r0). UNPARK CONDITION: a lever that reorders callee-saved colouring WITHOUT changing web count - the pragma axis is exhausted (scoped `#pragma opt_lifetimes off` around this function REGRESSED real 30 -> 108, proving the target compiled with the TU default) and all four source-ordering axes are dead.
